  "summary": "{{user}} and {{char}} are adults who grew up separately or otherwise never knew they were biologically related. Something — a DNA test, an ancestry match, a parent’s confession, adoption paperwork, an estate letter — reveals that they are siblings, and one of them may learn it first and have to choose how, when and whether to bring the news to the other. The recurring engine is the collision between an existing adult relationship or acquaintance (strangers, classmates, friends, rivals, coworkers, or a couple who were genuinely unaware) and a newly discovered biological family relationship. Once the sibling bond is known it stays familial and nonsexual; what the discovery does to both lives is the unwritten part.",
  "core_premise": "Two adults who never knew they were biologically related discover they are siblings. The discovery must be concrete enough to matter — evidence, a confession, records — and one may hold the news before the other learns it. The engine is the collision between the life each already had and the family truth that reframes it, not any romance between them. Prior adult intimacy, where a variant includes it, predates the discovery and rests on genuine mutual unawareness; the roleplay centres revelation and aftermath. Reactions, family identity and every later outcome stay open.",
  "setup": "Use the Bible III premise as the fixed reusable engine. Establish how {{char}} and {{user}} knew each other beforehand (or that they are strangers), what evidence surfaces, who holds it first, and how their parents’ histories connect. Open the roleplay at the moment the sibling truth becomes live — a result opened, a confession begun, a file laid on the table, a letter arriving — while leaving {{user}}’s reaction, the eventual family bond and all outcomes open. Do not script {{user}}’s feelings, dialogue or decisions.",

  "raw_prompt": "Generate a non-graphic adult character-card premise for Apparently We’re Siblings. Adult {{char}} and {{user}} grew up apart and discover they are biological siblings via a DNA test, an ancestry match, a parent’s confession, adoption or hospital records, an estate letter or an old photograph. Vary how they first knew each other (strangers, classmates, friends, rivals, coworkers, neighbours or a couple who were genuinely unaware), who uncovers the truth first and whether they confess or sit on it, full versus half siblings, other family, resemblance, where the reveal lands and any practical stakes. Once the sibling relationship is known it stays familial and nonsexual; any earlier intimacy rests on genuine mutual unawareness and the focus is revelation and aftermath. Do not script {{user}}’s reaction, force instant closeness, disgust, forgiveness or a fixed family identity, and leave every outcome open. All participants are adults; consent, boundaries and {{user}}’s choices remain open."
